title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on the Galois action on the profinite Teichmüller tower, circa 1978–81, before the Esquisse. On the preceding pages Grothendieck compares several 'graphs' I–VII, i.e. choices of base-point configurations and generating arcs on P^1 − {0,1,∞}. He computes the automorphisms of the profinite fundamental groupoid that fix the vertices and commute with the symmetries ρ (the order-3 rotation of 0,1,∞) and σ_∞ (an involution, probably the transposition fixing ∞, realized by complex conjugation and/or z ↦ 1/z type maps). On p.20 he has already reduced groupoid VII to parameters (λ, ξ') ∈ π̂_{0,3}^2 subject to (70). On this page he carries out that calculation explicitly.

The figure is the Riemann sphere with:
- two 'poles' P^+ and P^-, the upper and lower half-plane base points;
- the three punctures 0, 1, ∞ on the equator (the real line);
- around each puncture i a small circle carrying two base points R_i^+ and R_i^- (tangential-type points on either side of the real axis);
- half-loops a_i^± joining R_i^+ to R_i^- around the puncture;
- meridian arcs d̃_i^ω : P^ω → R_i^ω (same hemisphere) and d̃'_i^ω : P^ω → R_i^{ω'} (crossing to the other side), with ω ∈ {+,-} and ω' the opposite sign.

The groupoid is presented by these generators (71). The relations (72) are of two kinds:
- (a) d̃'_i^ω = a_i^ω d̃_i^ω, i.e. the triangle P^ω, R_i^ω, R_i^{ω'} is contractible. This expresses the d̃' in terms of the d̃ and a, or conversely a in terms of d̃ and d̃'.
- (b) A 4-cycle P^ω → R_i^ω → P^{ω'} → R_{ωi}^{ω'} → P^ω is trivial, where ωi is the neighbouring puncture in direction ω. This says each lune between consecutive meridians is a cell. There are six such relations, but only three are independent, because the relation for (i,ω) coincides with that for (ωi, ω'): it is the same cell.

So this is a cellular presentation of π_1(P^1 − 3 pts) adapted to the real structure, with S_3 × (conjugation) symmetry.

An equivariant automorphism u is written as u(d̃_i^ω) = φ_i^ω(ξ_1) d̃_i^ω, u(d̃'_i^ω) = φ_i^{ω'}(ξ') d̃'_i^ω and u(a_i^ω) = a_i^ω φ_i^ω(λ). Here φ_i^ω identifies the local group at the relevant base point with π̂_{0,3}, and by equivariance one uses the same ξ_1, ξ', λ for all i, ω. It remains to impose (72):
- (72a) gives (74): ξ' = ε_0(λ ξ_1), equivalently ξ_1 = λ^{-1} ε_0^{-1}(ξ'). Here ε_0 is the transition between local identifications.
- (72b) gives (75): β ξ_1 = β' τ_∞(ξ'), which serves to express β'.

On p.22 this becomes β' = α' σ_∞(λ) with α' = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1}, together with the constraint β' σ_∞(β') = 1. Earlier forms (70) and (70') also carry α' ρ(α') ρ²(α') = 1.

These are exactly the shapes of the 2-cycle relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1 and the 3-cycle relation of the Drinfeld–Ihara Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. The page is thus a step in deriving GT-type defining relations from symmetric base-point groupoids of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. The parameter λ attached to the half-loops a_i plays the role that the pair (χ(σ), conjugating element) plays in standard GT, where the inertia generator is conjugated and raised to a power.
errors: As transcribed, the first relation of (72), (d̃_i^{ω'})^{-1} a_i^ω d̃_i^ω = 1, does not typecheck: it is a path P^ω → P^{ω'} set equal to 1. It must be read as (d̃'_i^ω)^{-1} a_i^ω d̃_i^ω = 1, i.e. d̃'_i^ω = a_i^ω d̃_i^ω. That reading matches the side remark 'exprimant les d̃' en termes des d̃ et a'.

In (73) the left factors (crossed out) and the right factors are inconsistent across lines: the image shows φ(…) placed before d̃ in the first two lines but after a in the third. This is a convention issue (left vs right multiplication by local group elements) that Grothendieck partly corrects by crossing out.

(75) introduces β and τ_∞, which are not defined on this page; they presumably refer to (65) on an earlier page. On p.22 the relation is rewritten as β' = ξ_1 σ_∞(ξ')^{-1}, so τ_∞ vs σ_∞ notation is not stable.

ideas.what: Presentation of the profinite fundamental groupoid of P^1−{0,1,∞} on 8 base points: two half-plane points plus two points on either side of the real axis at each puncture. The sphere is cut along the real line and meridians into cells; relations come from the triangles and the lunes.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with several (tangential-type) base points; real/cellular decomposition of P^1−{0,1,∞}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 'groupoïdes fondamentaux à base points multiples'); Deligne 1989 (tangential base points); Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984): emphasis on fundamental groupoids with sets of base points stable under symmetries, and on the real-line/half-plane decomposition

ideas.what: Counting independent relations: six lune relations reduce to three, because the relation for (i,ω) equals that for (ωi, ω').

Parametrizing equivariant automorphisms (commuting with ρ of order 3 and the involution σ_∞) by elements λ, ξ_1, ξ' of π̂_{0,3}, and reducing the conditions to equations of the form β'σ_∞(β') = 1 and α'ρ(α')ρ²(α') = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Defining relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂ (2-cycle and 3-cycle relations)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse only alludes to describing Gal(Q̄/Q) via automorphisms of the tower; it gives no explicit relations

ideas.what: Half-loop parameter λ ∈ π̂_{0,3} attached to arcs joining the two tangential points at a puncture, used in place of an exponent in Ẑ.
ideas.modern_name: Half-inertia / paths between tangential base points on opposite sides of the real axis (as in 'real' versions of GT)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (cf. Nakamura; Lochak–Schneps on the S_3 / real-structure aspects)

missed.claim: An explicit, pre-Drinfeld derivation of GT-type relations (a 2-cycle relation β'σ_∞(β') = 1 and, nearby, a 3-cycle relation α'ρ(α')ρ²(α') = 1) for automorphisms of a symmetric multi-base-point groupoid of P^1−{0,1,∞}. The derivation proceeds by a cellular presentation along the real line with half-plane base points and paired points at each puncture.
missed.quote: six relations, mais il n'y en a que trois indépendantes, car l'équation pour i,ω et pour (ωi, ω') est la même.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck was writing down GT-like defining equations from equivariant groupoid presentations around 1978–81, before Drinfeld and Ihara. The particular 8-base-point, real-structure-adapted presentation, with an S_3 × conjugation symmetry and a π̂_{0,3}-valued half-loop parameter, is a variant not standard in the GT literature. It could be compared with GT variants built from different base-point choices.

missed.claim: The comparison of the automorphism groups of the graphs I–VII (diagram (68)) and the claim that some parameters are superfluous ('β' inutile', 'α' inutile') suggest a programme. The programme would show that the different base-point configurations yield the same (or comparable) GT-type group; it is only partially carried out here.
missed.quote: Je vais expliciter les calculs, dans le groupoïde VII
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Independence of GT from the choice of base-point configuration or groupoid model is folklore, but a systematic comparison of these specific models is not, to my knowledge, written out in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a genuine prefiguration of GT relations by Grothendieck in an unusual symmetric groupoid model. However, it is known from Schneps and others that his archive notes contain such computations. The page itself is routine bookkeeping toward those relations, with no final result stated here.
transcription_corrections: First line of (72): read (d̃'_i^ω)^{-1} a_i^ω d̃_i^ω = 1, with the prime on d and superscript ω, rather than (d̃_i^{ω'})^{-1}.
Second line of (72): read (d̃'^{ω}_{ωi})^{-1} d̃^{ω'}_{ωi} (d̃'^{ω'}_i)^{-1} d̃_i^ω = 1, a loop at P^ω.
Line 2 of the opening: 'mais en genre deux' is doubtful. The context is genus 0 (π̂_{0,3}), so 'genre deux' is very unlikely; the phrase is illegible.
(73): the parameters are ξ_1 (first line), ξ' (second line) and λ (third line), all in π̂_{0,3}. The image's 'ζ', ζ_1' corresponds to ξ', ξ_1.
